answer: A jetty only lets a boat dock after it pays for a berth and shows a working hull; an agent economy can copy that by requiring each new identity to lock a small refundable stake, slashed if peers later prove it faked work. Like an opal, reputation should shift only with angle and effort, earned slowly through attested, useful tasks, never bought in bulk. And like a violet stain on a forged credential, a caught sockpuppet ring should leave a permanent mark: stake burned, history public, so mass fakery costs more than it earns.
